title: Lavo Kingdom
capsule: The Lavo Kingdom (Lavapura) was a Mon-Khmer mandala centered at modern Lopburi on the left bank of the Chao Phraya River in central Thailand, attested from the 7th century and closely linked to the Dvaravati cultural sphere. By the 11th–12th centuries it fell under Khmer suzerainty and was absorbed into the Angkor imperial system, its rulers becoming subordinate governors. When the Tai Ayutthaya Kingdom rose in the mid-14th century, Lavo was gradually eclipsed and formally incorporated by 1388, ending its existence as a distinct polity.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Lavo's political existence is attested by inscriptions and Chinese records, but territorial boundaries are poorly defined given the fluid mandala polity structure; reconstruction depends heavily on archaeological distribution of Mon-style artifacts.
